Logical Venn diagrams + statement–conclusion reasoning. Draw the circles; never guess.

Only 3 Relationships Exist Between Sets

Every Venn question — and every syllogism — is built from these three bricks.

SUBSET — "All A are B"

Circle A sits fully inside B. All fathers are men; all apples are fruits.

OVERLAP — "Some A are B"

Circles cross — the lens between them is the "some". Some students are players.

DISJOINT — "No A is B"

Circles never touch. No dog is a cat; no pen is a pencil.

The Golden Rules of Syllogism

✅ All + All = All. All pens are books + all books are chairs → all pens are chairs.
✅ All A are B → at least Some B are A. (The subset always creates an overlap.)
❌ Some + Some = NO certain conclusion. Some boys are students + some students are players → we cannot conclude anything about boys and players.
❌ A negative statement (No…) never proves a positive "some" conclusion — but "No A is B" always gives "No B is A" (symmetry).
💡 Only a conclusion that is true in EVERY possible drawing follows. If you can sketch even one valid arrangement where it fails — it does not follow.
